episode_title: From Content Audits to Sonic Branding: Modern Marketing Tips with Michelle Ngome of AAMA

real_qa.q: What is sonic branding and how should marketers incorporate it into podcasts?
real_qa.r: Sonic branding refers to significant audio elements or jingles that make your podcast identifiable and recognizable. Michelle N'Gomey explains that certain apps and websites have distinctive sounds—like Spotify or McDonald's—that signal their brand. She recommends using a sonic branding hook in podcasts and short-form clips so listeners immediately know which podcast or creator they are hearing. This is especially valuable for short-form content distribution across platforms like TikTok and Reels.

real_qa.q: Why is content auditing and refreshing more important than creating new pages for B2B marketers?
real_qa.r: Michelle N'Gomey argues that if a website has more than 500 pages, marketers should conduct an audit and delete or refresh underperforming content rather than continuously create new pages. She recommends reviewing Google Analytics (GA4) to identify which content is performing and which is not, then refreshing high-potential pages quarterly or annually. This is a contrarian position at Content Marketing World—archiving articles is a viable strategy that gets overlooked in favor of always producing new content.

real_qa.q: How should marketers structure ChatGPT prompts to get better results than simple one-sentence queries?
real_qa.r: Rather than asking ChatGPT a single sentence like you would Google, marketers should provide more context and color. Michelle N'Gomey recommends including details such as location, target audience, and business objectives—for example, 'Pretend I am a marketer in Houston trying to reach entrepreneurs under 25 who are trying to do X, Y, and Z.' The language model learns more effectively with detailed prompts, and over time, shorter follow-up prompts become more valuable and tailored to your needs.
real_qa.requete: how to write ChatGPT prompts effectively

real_qa.q: What is Perplexity and how does it differ from ChatGPT for content research?
real_qa.r: Perplexity is a tool that combines ChatGPT with Google functionality. Unlike ChatGPT, when you enter prompts into Perplexity, it provides not only answers but also sources from which the information is drawn. This addresses a major issue with ChatGPT, where users cannot verify where the pulled information originated. Michelle N'Gomey discovered this tool and highlights that source attribution is critical when people are relying on AI responses as authoritative information.

real_qa.q: How can B2B marketers create engaging content from non-sexy industries using interactive approaches?
real_qa.r: Michelle N'Gomey shares an example of a cement company that transformed boring industry content into a comic book featuring employees as heroes. The team asked employees 'What is your superpower?' and turned their answers into creative hero personas, making company morale engaging and giving clients a new, funny perspective on account managers and employees. This approach extends account-based marketing beyond traditional dinner invitations to creative, differentiated touchpoints that require less budget but more imagination.

real_qa.q: Why did Michelle N'Gomey restart podcasting after stopping her previous show at 200 episodes?
real_qa.r: Michelle N'Gomey ran her first podcast for about five years and stopped at 200 episodes. When she founded the African American Marketing Association, she decided to start a new podcast because she recognized it was a strength her competitors did not have—they never launched one themselves. This unique offering became a core part of the association's value proposition, demonstrating that sometimes innovation is simply about doing something new that your competitors are not yet doing.
real_qa.requete: Michelle N'Gomey podcast African American Marketing Association

guest.bio_context: Michelle N'Gomey is based in Houston, Texas and founded the African American Marketing Association, a nonprofit designed to provide Black marketers with resources to grow their marketing careers and businesses. She also serves as Reach Director for Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses, a 14-week business program helping entrepreneurs scale, where she is responsible for recruiting entrepreneurs into the program.
